_doc: The anchor registry. One name for one control, whichever surface it is on.
ATTRIBUTE: data-coach. NOT health_learn's data-a — Payobook already had 40+
live data-coach anchors across six modules before this module existed, and
renaming them would churn every template for zero behaviour. The engine
reads one constant (engine/spotlight.js).
KINDS
product   the control exists in a real product template; data-coach="key"
must be found there verbatim. `screen` may be a LIST when one
template serves several screens (pb_payrun_ledgers renders Full
& Final, Proration and Retro from one file) — `shared: true`
marks that, so nobody reads a single-screen promise into it.
pattern   the control exists once PER RECORD. The template emits the key
with t-attf-data-coach, so the registry declares the prefix and
the test looks for that prefix rather than a literal key. Empty
in Phase A on purpose — see pk-card.
practice  a TEACHING view with no product counterpart: an arithmetic
breakdown, a lifecycle stepper, the replica's own navigation.
Named rep-* and declared so the gap is VISIBLE — the Coach must
never claim to point at one of these on a live screen.
foreign   data-coach anchors this module does not own. They belong to
pb_coach's tours and to PayAI, they predate pb_learn, and they
are listed so the lint can tell 'someone else's anchor' from
'a typo of one of ours'. Some entries are BOTH — pw-division,
pw-compute, the seven fs-* and, from Phase C1, the four dash-*:
the registry owns the name, pb_coach also points at it, and
neither module may rename one unilaterally.
tests/test_anchor_registry.py enforces every direction:
every product key exists in its template · every pattern prefix is
emitted · every practice key exists in the replica · every anchor the
content names is registered · every data-coach in a scanned file is
declared here or whitelisted as foreign · and the registry never silently
claims an anchor another module owns.

pw-rail.desc: The four-dot stepper. Where you are in the run, and what is still ahead.

pw-scope.desc: Period and batch name. The two inputs that decide which month is computed.

pw-division.desc: The division / formula configuration. Choosing it chooses the rulebook every payslip in this run is computed by.

pw-summary.desc: Company, configuration and eligible headcount. The last read before anything is computed.

pw-compute.desc: Compute payslips. Creates drafts only — nothing is paid, sent or approved.

pw-result.desc: What the compute produced: the run's name, its net total and its counts.

pw-pills.desc: Payslips / Computed / Need review. The third one is a question, not an error.

pw-exceptions.desc: The exceptions list — every payslip the engine wants a human to look at.

pk-kpis.desc: The KPI band above the board: total, in pipeline, awaiting YOUR approval, completed, net paid.

pk-run.desc: Run payroll. The same wizard the Run Payroll leaf opens, reached from the board.

pk-tabs.desc: Status tabs. They filter the board by approval stage, not by period.

pk-datechips.desc: Date chips. Every count above is scoped by whichever one is active.

pk-divchips.desc: Division chips. Shown only when this company runs payroll per division.

pk-card.desc: A pay run card. Emitted once per record, so a point-at lands on the first card on the board — enough to say 'a card looks like this', not enough to say 'that one'.

pk-card-actions.desc: The card's action footer. Which buttons appear is decided by the record's own gate fields, never by the card.

ps-runsel.desc: The run selector. Everything below it belongs to the run named here.

ps-kpis.desc: Payslips, net total, gross total, approved and need-review for this run.

ps-chips.desc: Filter chips: All / Need review / HR pending / GM pending / Done.

ps-list.desc: The payslip list. A flag dot marks a slip the engine wants read.

ps-detail.desc: The detail pane for the selected employee.

ps-status.desc: The approval stepper. It is the payslip's own position in the chain, not the run's.

ps-breakdown.desc: Salary breakdown, line by line with its rule code. The working behind the net figure.

im-kpis.desc: Batches, completed, in progress, with errors, connectors.

im-cta.desc: Start an import. Opens the guided wizard — the only path that scores a file before it commits.

im-launches.desc: The secondary launches: the older per-tool import surfaces.

im-pipe.desc: map → validate → commit. A batch that stops before commit has changed nothing.

im-batches.desc: Recent batches and their state. Where you go back to a file that stalled.

iw-steps.desc: The wizard's stepper: source, review & match, validate & fix, commit.

iw-source.desc: Where the data comes from, and which formula configuration reads it.

iw-review.desc: Rows loaded, matched, new and needing attention. The confidence read before any fix.

iw-fixrows.desc: Match / Retry / Skip. Fixing the INPUT here is what stops a wrong payslip later.

iw-outcome.desc: What the commit actually created: employees and payslips.

iw-commit.desc: Commit import. The first irreversible control in this flow — everything before it is a preview.

lg-kpis.desc: The ledger KPI band. ONE template serves Full & Final, Proration Audit and Retro Adjustments, so this key means a different set of numbers on each — the screen key decides which.

lg-facets.desc: The facet chips and the date row. Same control, different facets per ledger.

lg-rows.desc: The ledger rows. Each is a line of working, not a record to edit.

lg-openfull.desc: Open full list. Leaves the cockpit for the underlying list view.

fs-config.desc: The configuration switcher. Its name IS the rulebook a division is paid by — reading it is how you know which config you are editing.

fs-components.desc: The component outline: every named piece of the rulebook, in four kinds. A payslip line exists because a component here produced it.

fs-formula.desc: The formula itself, as coloured chips. Each chip is a component you can click through to; the colour is its kind.

fs-namesletters.desc: Names / Letters. One formula in two spellings — names to explain it, letters to read it beside a spreadsheet.

fs-deps.desc: Depends on / Used by. The blast radius of a rename or a deletion, written down before you make one.

fs-preview.desc: The live preview: the whole configuration evaluated against one sample employee, line by line.

fs-simulate.desc: Simulate. Runs the edited configuration against a period that has already been paid — the evidence the one-employee preview is not.

st-new.desc: New insurance policy. A rate change is a NEW RECORD with its own code and effective date; there is no version chain to edit.

st-kpis.desc: Contributions, employee leg, employer leg, policies, tax tables, dependents.

st-rates.desc: The active insurance rates table: scheme, employee share, employer share and ceiling. The near end of L6's trace — the 1.5% that becomes a deduction.

st-effective.desc: The effective date of the policy on display. The field that decides which rates a payslip is computed with, and the whole of the risk in changing one.

st-slabs.desc: The progressive thuế TNCN bands for the active tax year.

st-filters.desc: Insurance policies / tax tables, and the active-only chip. Every count in the roster below is scoped by these.

st-roster.desc: The policy roster. Two rows is the healthy shape: a rate change ends one record and starts another, so the list reads as a history.

sr-new.desc: New structure. Present, and almost always the wrong control: new pay logic belongs in a formula configuration.

sr-kpis.desc: Structures, salary rules, categories, employees covered and countries.

sr-filters.desc: Status, search, date and country chips. They scope the roster, not the database.

sr-roster.desc: The structure cards. Each is history: the rule set a payslip from before the migration was computed by.

sr-openall.desc: Open full structures list. Leaves the cockpit for the underlying list view.

ig-connect.desc: Connect a system. Adds a source payroll data can arrive from without anybody retyping it.

ig-kpis.desc: Connectors, connected, errors, synced records, field mappings and staged records.

ig-filters.desc: Status, search, recency and type chips over the connector roster.

ig-roster.desc: The connector cards, with the last-sync time and the staged count. A connector that stopped still says connected — the sync time is the tell.

st-newpolicy-date.desc: The effective date on the new-policy wizard. It is the company's record of when a rate change legally started — read by auditors and by the statutory reports, and NOT a switch: the cockpit displays the latest-dated active policy the moment it is saved.

dash-hero.desc: The dashboard hero: who you are, which run is live, and how much of it is done. The first sentence Payobook says to anybody who logs in.

dash-kpis.desc: Headcount, monthly payroll, pending approvals and active configurations. Four numbers that describe the company, not the day.

dash-runpayroll.desc: Run Payroll, from the hero. The same wizard the sidebar leaf opens — the dashboard is a way in, never a second way of doing it.

dash-formula.desc: The formula engine card. Payobook computes pay from readable configurations rather than fixed structures, and this is where the dashboard says so.

pa-hero.desc: The approval pipeline header, with the count that is waiting on YOU. Officer review, then HR review, then Finance approval, printed in order.

pa-kpis.desc: How many runs sit at each gate, and the net at stake across all of them. A money figure that has not been paid and can still be stopped.

pa-lanes.desc: The three lanes and the run cards in them. A card offers Approve and Reject only at the gate you hold; everywhere else it names who is holding it up.

pa-recent.desc: Recently decided, approvals and rejections together, with the written reason on every rejection. The audit trail as a reading surface.

pa-reject.desc: The reject popover. The reason field is required, and the note beneath it says what rejecting does to the payslips in the run.

pe-head.desc: The Employees header and its two actions: Select, which turns on bulk mode, and Add employee.

pe-bulk.desc: The bulk bar. Visible only in select mode, and the one control on this screen that changes many records at once.

pe-kpis.desc: Headcount, running contracts, contracts expiring within 30 days, new hires this month, the monthly wage bill and the payroll-ready share.

pe-filters.desc: Status chips, search and the date range. Every count above is scoped by whatever is active here.

pe-roster.desc: The employee cards: job, department, wage, contract expiry and the payroll-ready tick. Read the tick before a run, not after it.

ct-head.desc: The Contracts header. A separate screen from Employees on purpose: a person is not a contract, and payroll is paid from the contract.

ct-kpis.desc: Running, expiring within 30 days, draft, expired, the monthly wage bill and the average wage.

ct-filters.desc: Status chips, search and the date range over the contract roster.

ct-roster.desc: The contract cards, each with its period and its wage. The expiry chip is the one to read in the week before a run.

in-hero.desc: The headline figure and the run it was read from. Every number on this board is a door back to where it came from.

in-trend.desc: The cost story over three, six or twelve months. A trend answers a different question from a total, and the window chip decides which.

in-duo.desc: Department leaderboard and the statutory split, side by side: where the cost sits, and how much of it is the law rather than salary.

in-pulse.desc: Workforce pulse — attendance exceptions and headcount movement for this week and month to date.

in-explore.desc: Ask something else. The way out of a board that has answered every question it anticipated, into the Explorer.

ex-head.desc: The Explorer header. A question builder rather than a report: pick a measure, break it down, filter it.

ex-rail.desc: The chip rail: measure, breakdown and comparison. The three choices that define the question being asked.

ex-filters.desc: The Where group — every active filter as a removable tag. A figure read without checking this is a figure read out of scope.

ex-headline.desc: The result headline: the measure, the dimension it is broken down by, and the total the table sums to.

ex-table.desc: The result table. Rows are the breakdown, columns are the comparison — and it reconciles with the payslips it was derived from.

wa-head.desc: The Workforce Insights header. Attendance, overtime, leave and cost per head, read off payroll rather than off a separate HR system.

wa-filters.desc: Division and period pickers. They scope every panel below, which is why an alarming number is worth re-reading with these in view.

wa-kpis.desc: Employees paid, joiners and leavers, and the cost per head. Employees PAID, not employed — the difference is the point.

wa-chart.desc: Headcount paid, month by month. A step in this line is a joiner wave, a leaver wave, or a run that did not include everybody.

wa-duo.desc: Attendance exceptions beside overtime. Two panels because the second is usually the consequence of the first.

gr-head.desc: The filings header, naming the company, its country and the month being filed for. The period control is a month, not a date range.

gr-countries.desc: The country chips. Shown only when this company runs payroll in more than one country, because the filings are the country's, not Payobook's.

gr-grid.desc: The report tiles, grouped by the authority that asks for them. Each opens the existing wizard prefilled with the company and the period.

gr-empty.desc: The honest empty state: this country's filings are not built yet. Better than a tile that generates a form nobody can submit.

practice.rep-nav: The replica's own sidebar. Mirrors pb_sidebar; nothing on it navigates the real app.
practice.rep-banner: The practice banner. Says, on every screen, that none of this is your company.
practice.rep-dash-runs: The replica Dashboard's three-month run list. The product draws ONE latest-run card here; three months is a teaching view, so it keeps a rep- name and the Coach must never claim to point at it on a live screen.
practice.rep-pipeline: The lifecycle stepper: draft → level0 → level1 → level2 → done, with the rejection branch. A teaching view; the product draws this as columns, not as a stepper.
practice.rep-slipline: The worked example's statutory deductions, drawn on the STATUTORY replica beside the rates that produced them. It is the far end of L6's trace and it exists only here: the product's statutory cockpit shows rates, and a payslip shows đồng, and no single product screen shows both at once. Naming it rep- is the honest consequence — the Coach must never claim to point at this on a live screen.

foreign.pw-division: pb_coach — hero_path.js, tour_payrun.js. ALSO ours: the registry owns it and neither module may rename it alone.
foreign.pw-compute: pb_coach — hero_path.js, tour_payrun.js. ALSO ours, same rule.
foreign.dash-hero: pb_dashboard / pb_coach hero_path. ALSO ours from Phase C1: LW names it, the registry owns it, and neither module may rename it alone.
foreign.dash-kpis: pb_dashboard / pb_coach hero_path. ALSO ours from Phase C1, same rule.
foreign.dash-formula: pb_dashboard / pb_coach hero_path. ALSO ours from Phase C1, same rule.
foreign.dash-runpayroll: pb_dashboard. ALSO ours from Phase C1 — no tour points at this one, so it is promoted on the fs-simulate terms: in the template, named by a lesson, owned by the registry.
foreign.fs-*: pb_formula_studio — the Formula Studio tours. SEVEN of these are PROMOTED into `product` above (fs-config, fs-components, fs-formula, fs-namesletters, fs-deps, fs-preview, fs-simulate): pb_learn's L5 names them, so the registry owns them and a rename breaks a build rather than a lesson. pb_coach's hero_path and tour_formula point at six of the seven, so — exactly like pw-division and pw-compute — neither module may rename one alone. Everything else matching fs-* is still someone else's.
foreign.imp-*: pb_hr_payroll_formula — the multi-sheet import wizard tour
